content.value: Runes add bonuses to eligible equipment. A rune has an affix side, a tier and rolled values. Its family describes the kind of improvement; its tier and roll determine how strong that improvement is.
Find compatible equipment with runes already on it, or roll a random family with a suitable tome at the [[article/runic_altar|Runic Altar]].
Use a [[article/targeted_tomes|specialized tome]] when you want a known family. Click its listed rune to inspect its effect, tier values, compatible bases and the tier that tome can give.
Use an [[article/artificial_tome|Artificial Tome]] to reveal a choice between compatible results. It requires the Runic Altar first and the Artificial Runic Altar to reveal the choice.

Magic equipment holds one prefix and one suffix. Rare equipment holds three of each. A hybrid rune may grant several stats but still occupies one slot. Bonuses joined by a bracket in the equipment tooltip belong to that same rune.

An item cannot keep two runes of the same family. Different values or different tiers do not make a second copy legal. A hybrid is its own family, so read its article when comparing it with a single-stat rune.
Flat item bonuses add to the matching equipment property. Local increases then improve that item before your character-wide bonuses are evaluated.

For example, an item with 10 base Physical Damage and +5 flat Physical Damage reaches 18 item damage with 20% local increased Physical Damage: (10 + 5) × 1.2 = 18. Quality improves the original base before the flat rune is added.
The equipment tooltip already shows its local improvements. Do not add the rune to that final displayed value again. Tree bonuses can then improve the applicable character or attack total.

A stronger material allows stronger tiers. Adding rarity or spending a stronger tome cannot bypass that cap. The [[item/minecraft:mace|Mace]], [[item/minecraft:trident|Trident]], [[item/minecraft:turtle_helmet|Turtle Helmet]] and [[item/minecraft:elytra|Elytra]] have fixed Unique properties; tools and animal armour also do not accept ordinary rune affixes.

Decide which problem you need to solve before spending a tome: damage type, survival, recovery or a missing requirement. A new rune is useful only if the rest of the build can use it. Inspect the proposed result before replacing a valuable rune.
